reuse.why: The category selection is consolidated and reuses extractTagsFromText, but setLastMonthSpending computes last month's spending with its own transactions SQL instead of reading the existing 'sum-amount-<cat>' sheet cell via getSheetValue that getCategoryAverage already uses.

duplication.why: Four copies of the category query collapse into getFillableCategories; the new action re-derives spending in SQL and every action still repeats the income/tracking guard.

placement.why: The selection helper and new action live in budget/actions.ts with the other month-wide actions and the method is registered in app.ts next to its siblings; the raw transaction aggregation in the action layer is somewhat out of place.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, the new handler registration and release notes are touched.

maintainability.why: One selection function owns the hidden/fixed/template rules with an explicit includeHiddenCategories parameter, though the income rule stays per action and the bespoke spending query (fixed day 31 range, offbudget join) is a second definition of spending to keep in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts setLastMonthSpending: SUM over v_transactions_internal_alive instead of the sheet 'sum-amount-' cell read by getSheetValue/getCategoryAverage

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending's transaction SUM query is a reshaped re-derivation of the per-month spending the budget sheet already exposes as sum-amount-<category>

abstraction_drift.where: getFillableCategories gained the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter (conditional WHERE clause); all five month-wide actions, including copyPreviousMonth via an id set, go through it; income-in-tracking guard remains duplicated at each call site
